review_notes: I read the whole target file, the defining file CoreDensityTranslation.lean (thermalCoordinates, thermalPoint, thermalCoordinates_apply, thermalPoint_eq_center, clamped_thermalPoint_measurable), and grepped for uses of these lemmas. I did not find any simp attributes in the file, so there are no competing rules or loops. The findings are about a missing canonical rewrite interface: the component lemmas are not packaged as simp lemmas, and the same unfolding simp set is repeated by hand. I did not run Lean. I did not check whether `rfl` after the simp calls is robust, and I did not check whether adding `@[simp]` would clash with the `local irreducible` setup in CoreJointParameterDensity.lean. This is a modest, low-severity interface issue.

findings.problem: These two lemmas are the component-wise normal form of `thermalPoint`: transverse is `d • transverse (toLp 2 w)` and axial is `axialMap … (w 2)`. They are plain theorems and are used only through explicit `rw`. The same unfolding recipe (thermalPoint, thermalCoordinates_apply, velocityMap, and the join lemmas) is retyped in other places. thermalPoint_eq_center repeats it, and clamped_thermalPoint_measurable unfolds `thermalPoint` the same way. Each new proof about `transverse`/`axial` of a thermal point has to rediscover this four-lemma simp set. The `rfl` after `simp only` in the axial lemma also depends on the unfolding details. This is a missing canonical rewrite interface.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `thermalPoint_transverse` and `thermalPoint_axial` as `@[simp]`. Both are safe: the LHS is `transverse (thermalPoint …)` or `axial (thermalPoint …)`, the RHS has no `thermalPoint`, and they cannot loop. Place them directly after the definitions, together with `thermalCoordinates_apply`, so that thermalPoint_eq_center and the clamped-measurability proof can use them instead of unfolding `thermalPoint` and `velocityMap`. Alternatively, state a single `thermalPoint_eq` as `split (thermalPoint …) = (d • transverse (toLp 2 w), axialMap … (w 2))`.
findings.benefit: Callers can reduce `transverse`/`axial` of a thermal point with plain `simp`, without opening `thermalPoint`/`velocityMap`. The unfolding recipe then lives in one place, so proofs stay stable if `velocityMap` or `thermalCoordinates` is refactored.

findings.problem: `thermalCoordinates_apply` is the only unfolding lemma for `thermalCoordinates`. It is not tagged `@[simp]`, so every `simp only` list in this file and in CoreDensityTranslation.lean has to name it explicitly (lines 19, 25, 76, 185, 221). A bare `simp` or `simp [thermalPoint]` therefore leaves `thermalCoordinates w` opaque. Its RHS, `(transverse (toLp 2 w), axial (toLp 2 w))`, is a more canonical form than the `join.symm` definition.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `thermalCoordinates_apply`, since the RHS contains no `thermalCoordinates`. Together with simp lemmas for `thermalPoint_transverse` and `thermalPoint_axial`, this lets the two proofs here shrink to `by simp` or a short `simp [JetCoreMeasure.velocityMap]`. Check that it does not interfere with the `local irreducible thermalPoint` setup in CoreJointParameterDensity.lean.
findings.benefit: Fewer hand-maintained simp lists, and `simp` can normalise thermal coordinates to a `(transverse, axial)` pair.
